factories.name: new_query_step
factories.description: Run one parameterized statement in a read-only transaction and return its bounded rows.

inputSchema.description: QueryRowsInput is one parameterized read statement.

parameters.description: Parameters binds $1 through $n in order. Each value is nil for SQL NULL, a string, bool, integer, float, json.Number, json.RawMessage, []byte for bytea, or time.Time, and is sent as text that PostgreSQL parses for the type it infers for that placeholder. Pass exact decimals and integers beyond 2^53 as strings or json.Number.

statement.description: Statement is one SQL statement written as a constant in application code, such as "SELECT id, plan FROM subscriptions WHERE account_email = $1". Values belong in Parameters: the connector never formats them into SQL text, and it cannot detect a statement built by concatenating untrusted input. Transaction control and COPY are rejected before any request.

factories.name: new_execute_step
factories.description: Run one parameterized write statement in its own transaction and return its rows affected and bounded RETURNING rows.

inputSchema.description: ExecuteStatementInput is one parameterized write statement.

idempotencyKeyPlaceholder.description: IdempotencyKeyPlaceholder, when non-zero, is the number n of the $n placeholder that receives this Step execution's idempotency key. It must equal len(Parameters)+1, so the key is always the last placeholder. The key is a UUID that stays the same across every retry and Worker replacement of one Step execution, and it is also returned in the Result's Receipt.

maxRowsAffected.description: MaxRowsAffected, when set, is the most rows the statement may affect. A statement that affects more is rolled back and selects limitExceeded, which guards against a missing WHERE clause. Nil applies no limit; zero allows only a statement that changes nothing.

parameters.description: Parameters binds $1 through $n in order, with the same value rules as QueryRowsInput.

statement.description: Statement is one SQL statement written as a constant in application code, such as "INSERT INTO refunds (order_id, amount) VALUES ($1, $2::numeric)". Values belong in Parameters: the connector never formats them into SQL text, and it cannot detect a statement built by concatenating untrusted input. Transaction control and COPY are rejected before any request. A RETURNING clause returns rows in the Result.
